title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook (Comprehensive)
author: Daniel Park
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standardized on-call and incident response process. It covers incident classification, lifecycle and handoffs, runbook templates for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation rules, game day guidance, and both internal status-page and customer-facing communication templates. The goal is to keep incident handling predictable, fast, and blameless while ensuring customers are informed and engineering teams learn from failures.

1) Roles & Responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): owns triage decisions, customer comms cadence, and post-incident follow-up until handoff.
- Primary on-call: first responder for alerts, performs initial triage and mitigation steps.
- Secondary on-call: escalation target if primary is unavailable or incident requires additional bandwidth.
- SRE/Platform on-call: responsible for infra, routing, autoscaler, and capacity issues.
- Product/CS liaison: drafts customer-facing messages for paid customers and coordinates QBR-level escalations.
- PagerDuty/communication owner: maintains escalation policies and contact lists.

2) Incident Severity Matrix (for-routing and SLOs)
| Severity | Symptoms | Target MTTA | Target MTTD | Example triggers |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Sev 1 (P1) | Global outage, major feature broken affecting >50% requests | 5m | 15m | API 5xx rate >30% cluster-wide, state-store degraded |
| Sev 2 (P2) | Major degradation for a subset of customers or regions | 15m | 60m | Elevated token latency, regional routing failure |
| Sev 3 (P3) | Feature regression for small set; throughput/latency within SLOs | 1 business day | 1 business day | Quality regression reproducible on canary prompts |

3) Incident Lifecycle (high-level)
1. Detection: Automated alert or customer report. Provide alert context (runbook link, metrics, recent deploys).
2. Triage (0-15m): Primary on-call assesses severity using the matrix, assigns IC if P1/P2.
3. Mitigation (0-60m): Apply runbook steps to restore service or reduce customer impact (fallback models, scale-up, regional failover).
4. Communication (ongoing): IC updates internal channel every 15-30 minutes for P1/P2; publish status updates to status.redwood.ai if external impact.
5. Containment & Recovery: Verify full recovery, monitor for regressions for at least 2x the incident duration.
6. Postmortem & Action Items: Draft a blameless postmortem within 72 hours (for P1/P2) and implement action items with owners and deadlines.

4) Triage Checklist (first responder)
- Gather context: recent deploys, changelogs, alert graphs (latency, 5xx rate), affected regions/customers.
- Identify scope: percentage of traffic, single service vs multi-service, single region vs global.
- Run quick mitigations: scale up, roll back last deploy, enable fallback model, disable risky feature flags.
- Escalate to IC if severity is P1/P2 or if initial mitigation fails within 15 minutes.

5) Runbook Templates (copyable sections)
A) API 5xx spike / high error rate
- Symptoms: 5xx rate >10% sustained for 5m, user complaints of failures.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Check service health dashboards: ingress, upstreams, queue lengths.
  2) Check recent deploys: if a rollout is within last 30m, consider rollback procedure.
  3) Scale ingress/worker pods by +2x (or follow autoscaler override guide).
  4) If errors originate from a downstream dependency, toggle degraded-mode feature flags.
  5) If root cause unclear after 15m, escalate to Platform SRE.
  6) Draft internal update with ETA.
  7) If customer impact crosses P1 threshold, publish status page update (see templates).

B) GPU OOM / Model OOM on Dedicated Nodes
- Symptoms: OOM crashes, repeated model restarts, elevated retry loops.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Identify affected model/version and node pool.
  2) Drain node from serving pool for investigation.
  3) Switch traffic to compatible lower-memory quantized variant if available.
  4) Increase node pool capacity or move traffic to Dedicated bursting pool.
  5) Collect and attach core dumps/logs to ticket; escalate to runtime/kernel team if OOM reproducible on deterministic inputs.

C) KV-cache corruption / prefix-cache inconsistency
- Symptoms: Wrong completions, cache-miss spikes, increased cold-start latency.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Isolate cache shard(s) showing anomalies.
  2) Flush affected shard(s) with coordinated rolling flush.
  3) Rebuild prefixes from persisted logs if available.
  4) Put guarded traffic on fresh cache warmup policy for 30-60m.

6) Escalation Paths & PagerDuty Rules
- P1: PagerDuty -> Primary on-call (Page) + IC Slack channel ping -> If no ack in 5 minutes, page Secondary + SRE lead.
- P2: Primary on-call page -> if no ack in 15 minutes, page Secondary.
- P3: Ticket created in JIRA with on-call assignment; no immediate paging.
- All escalations must be reflected in the incident ticket with timestamps and who was paged.

7) On-call Rotations & Handoffs
- Rotation length: 1 week for platform/SRE on-call; 2 weeks for product and runtime on-call to reduce context-switch cost.
- Handoff checklist (incoming): review open incidents/incidents-in-watch, read the last 24h of runbook updates, confirm contact details, and verify access to dashboards and runbooks.
- Handoff checklist (outgoing): summarize outstanding issues, active mitigations, and pending action items in the oncall channel and close or reassign short tasks.
- Emergency replacements: if a primary cannot attend, primary must notify secondary and update PagerDuty schedule at least 24h in advance.

8) Game Days (purpose & plan)
- Goal: exercise runbooks, validate automation, and train ICs in a low-risk environment.
- Frequency: quarterly for major services; monthly mini-game-days for new features.
- Typical agenda:
  1) Pre-brief: objectives, success criteria, participant roles.
  2) Inject: synthetic alert (e.g., regional routing failure, model regression).
  3) Execute: follow playbook, time-to-mitigation targets measured.
  4) Debrief: 30-60m review, lessons learned, and ticketed follow-ups.
- Metrics captured: MTTA, MTTD, time-to-recovery, and checklist adherence.

9) Postmortem & Learning Process
- Postmortem must be written within 72h for P1/P2 incidents and include: timeline, impact, root cause analysis (RCA), contributing factors, blameless narrative, action items with owners and due dates, and verification plan.
- Severity mapping to postmortem type:
  - P1/P2: full postmortem with root cause and remediation plan.
  - P3: short incident summary and follow-up if recurring.
- Postmortem template (use as a checklist):
  - Title, incident start/end, summary (one paragraph), impact (customers/region/metrics), timeline (timestamped events), RCA (why), Contributing factors, Action items (owner + due date), Follow-up validation steps, Lessons learned.

10) Status Page & Customer Communication Templates
A) Internal status update (IC -> #incidents channel)
- [TIMESTAMP] Sev{1|2} detected: short summary.
- Affected: services/regions/customers.
- Current status: Mitigating / Degraded / Recovering / Resolved.
- Actions taken: list of steps.
- Next update ETA: +15m.

B) Public status page update (short-form)
- Title: [Investigating | Identified | Monitoring | Resolved] - brief description
- Impact: who is affected (e.g., all API requests in us-west-2)
- Current status: what we have done and next steps
- ETA: estimate for next update or resolution if known
- Example: "Investigating - increased 5xx rate for text-generation API in us-west-2. We are routing traffic away from an affected pool and investigating a recent rollout. Next update in 15 minutes."

C) Customer-facing email template (for impacted paid customers)
- Subject: Redwood Inference Incident: [Short summary] - [In progress / Resolved]
- Body:
  1) What happened (concise): e.g., starting at 14:05 UTC we observed elevated 5xx errors affecting API calls routed through us-west-2.
  2) Impact: services/customers affected and mitigation status.
  3) What we are doing: specific mitigations and timeline.
  4) Next update: ETA for next message and channel (status.redwood.ai).
  5) Post-incident followup: commit to a postmortem and direct contact for high-touch support if needed.

11) Operational Tooling & Dashboards (minimum dashboards to check)
- Global ingress dashboard: 5xx rate, latency p50/p95/p99, request volume.
- Model-serving health: queue length, worker cpu/gpu utilization, OOM rate.
- Cache metrics: prefix hit-rate, cold-start rate, rebuild time.
- Autoscaler & capacity: pending scale requests, node pool utilization, burst capacity usage.

12) Runbook Ownership & Maintenance
- Each runbook must list an owner and a last-reviewed date. Runbooks must be reviewed at least quarterly or after any incident where they were used.
- Use the following metadata in the runbook header: owner, secondary, last_reviewed, criticality, and related playbooks.

13) Appendices
- Rollback checklist (safe rollback steps, how to pin traffic and verify): 1) Pause rollout, 2) Pin stable model version, 3) Warm caches, 4) Monitor for degradation.
- Example Slack incident channel naming: #inc-ind-{YYYYMMDD}-{short-title}
- Example JIRA labels: incident, sev1, postmortem, oncall

If you have feedback or updates to suggest, open a PR against this page or contact the eng-sre rotation lead.
